'''Mary Arlene Appelhof''' (June 11, 1936 &ndash; May 4, 2005) was an American [[biologist]], vermicomposter, and [[environmentalist]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nwhp.org/resourcecenter/biographycenter.php |title=National Women's History Project |publisher=Nwhp.org |date= |accessdate=2013-12-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006182616/http://www.nwhp.org/resourcecenter/biographycenter.php |archive-date=2014-10-06 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Her 1982 book ''[[Worms Eat My Garbage]]'' is still held as seminal reading in the field of [[vermicomposting]].<ref name="grist">{{cite news |last1=Kwak-Hefferan |first1=Elisabeth K |title=What worms eat for breakfast |url=https://grist.org/food/2011-10-06-what-worms-eat-for-breakfast/ |accessdate=15 December 2019 |publisher=Grist |date=6 October 2011}}</ref><ref name="tolbert">{{cite news |last1=Tolbert |first1=Kathryn |title=She started composting. Who knew red wigglers and worm poop were so interesting? |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/health-science/she-started-composting-who-knew-red-wigglers-and-worm-poop-were-so-interesting/2017/04/21/d7406864-0a8c-11e7-93dc-00f9bdd74ed1_story.html |accessdate=15 December 2019 |newspaper=The Washington Post |date=22 April 2017}}</ref><ref name="postalwait">{{cite news |last1=Postalwait |first1=Chris |title=Good to Grow: Compost kitchen waste three times faster with worms |url=https://www.wvgazettemail.com/life/gardening/good-to-grow-compost-kitchen-waste-three-times-faster-with/article_99ecc5cd-ca92-5d16-b964-8b6905d6913a.html |accessdate=15 December 2019 |publisher=Charleston Gazette-Mail |date=29 March 2019}}</ref><ref name="bestpractices">{{cite web |last1=McBride |first1=Angus |last2=Muturi |first2=Caroline |last3=Githiri |first3=David |last4=Parker |first4=Julian |title=Tiger Worm Toilets - Best Practice Guidelines for Refugee Camps |url=https://www.humanitarianlibrary.org/sites/default/files/2018/12/Tiger%20Worm%20Toilets%20Best%20Practice%20Guidelines%20%28Oxfam%20and%20UNHCR%202017%29%20PDF.pdf |website=humanitarianlibrary |date=2017 |accessdate=16 December 2019}}</ref> In 2009 she was designated a [[Women's History Month]] Honoree by the [[National Women's History Project]].<ref name="WHM">{{cite web | author= | year=2010 | title=Honorees: 2010 National Women's History Month | work=Women's History Month | publisher=[[National Women's History Project]] | url=http://nwhp.org/whm/honorees.php | accessdate=14 November 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110624015034/http://nwhp.org/whm/honorees.php | archive-date=24 June 2011 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Family and education ==
Mary Appelhof was born in [[Detroit]], Michigan. Her father was Pastor of St. John Episcopal Church in [[Alma, Ohio]] and St. Thomas Episcopal Church in [[Berea, Ohio]].<ref name=Hilda>{{cite web|title=Hilda Whiteley Appelhof|url=http://www.migenweb.org/grandtraverse/obits-w.html|work=Grand Traverse County Deaths & Obits|accessdate=24 Jan 2013|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304024347/http://www.migenweb.org/grandtraverse/obits-w.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>  In 1954 she graduated from Berea High School in Berea, Ohio and in 1958 graduated from [[Michigan State University]] in [[East Lansing]], Michigan with a B.S. in biology.<ref name="Gazette Obit">{{cite news|title=APPELHOF, Mary Arlene: Newspaper Obituary and Death Notice|newspaper=Kalamazoo Gazette|date=10 May 2005}}</ref> In 1959 Appelhof graduated from Michigan State University with an M.S. degree in biology.<ref name="Gazette Obit" />  She later earned an M.S. degree in education and studied advanced biology.{{cn|date=March 2025}}

Appelhof had many talents, including expert swimming and award-winning nature photography.<ref name=Legacy>{{cite web|last=Walker|first=Emily|title='Worm woman' leaves a legacy of teaching about environment|url=http://www.wormwoman.com/acatalog/wormwoman.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170620041624/http://www.wormwoman.com/acatalog/wormwoman.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2017-06-20|work=In Memoriam}}</ref> She taught science at Kalamazoo Central High School in [[Kalamazoo]], Michigan and taught at Interlochen Arts Academy in Interlochen, Michigan.{{cn|date=March 2025}}

== Designing and promoting worm systems ==
In the early 1970s, Appelhof began experimenting with worms and organic waste.  Her home worm container would become  a new career.<ref name="Bio Day" />

<blockquote>Her vision at the time of the Stockholm Conference for the Human Environment (1972) was "tons of worms could be eating tons of garbage."<ref name="Bio Day" /></blockquote>
  
Soon she was publicly advocating using the earthworm to recycle [[food waste]].<ref name="Bio Day">{{cite web|title=mary arlene appelhof "the worm woman"|url=http://www.democraticunderground.com/11381458|work=A Biography of the Day|accessdate=24 Jan 2013}}</ref>  
As "Worm Woman," she introduced thousands of schoolchildren and home gardeners to [[vermicomposting]].
She was awarded a [[National Science Foundation]] grant to do videomicroscopy of live worms.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.emilycompost.com/mary_appelhof.htm |title=Celebrating gardening, plants, and weeds |publisher=EmilyCompost |accessdate=2013-12-27 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005055957/http://www.emilycompost.com/mary_appelhof.htm |archivedate=2013-10-05 }}</ref><ref name="in Memory">{{cite web|title=In Memory of Mary Appelhof – The Worm Women|url=http://www.compost-bin.org/mary-appelhof/|work=The Compost Bin|accessdate=24 Jan 2013|archive-date=19 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219022758/http://www.compost-bin.org/mary-appelhof/|url-status=dead}}</ref> This resulted in a DVD "Wormania."<ref name="in Memory" /><ref name=Wormania>{{cite web|title=Wormania|url=http://www.wormwoman.com/acatalog/Wormwoman_catalog_Wormania__33.html|work=Flowerfield Enterprises|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130112023810/http://www.wormwoman.com/acatalog/Wormwoman_catalog_Wormania__33.html|archivedate=2013-01-12}}</ref>

== Flower Press ==
Appelhof purchased  an old [[mimeograph]] machine from the Democratic Party in the early 1970s.<ref name="flower field MAA bio">{{cite web|title=Mary Appelhof|url=http://www.wormwoman.com/acatalog/articles.html|work=Flowerfield Enterprises Articles|accessdate=25 Jan 2013}}</ref>  She used it  to produce  a brochure,  "Basement Worm Bins Produce Potting Soil and Reduce Garbage."<ref name="flower field MAA bio" />  By 1976  her publishing interests  were firm, and she founded Flower Press.   She later explained  her thoughts on self-publishing her bestseller,  ''Worms Eat My Garbage.''<ref name="worms eat">{{cite book|last=Appelhof|first=Mary|title=Worms Eat My Garbage|year=1976|publisher=Flower Press|location=Kalamazoo, MI}}</ref>

<blockquote>My goal, however, was not to make lots of money, but to influence people's thinking. To get them to think differently about waste, and give them tools to deal with it. Self-publishing my book was the way I could do that. So I learned what I had to learn to be able to do so.<ref name="self publish">{{cite web|last=Appelhof|first=Mary|title=Why I Chose to Self- Publish|url=http://www.wormwoman.com/acatalog/self_publish.html|work=Flowerfield Enterprises|accessdate=25 Jan 2013}}</ref></blockquote>

*''Worms Eat Our Garbage: Classroom Activities for a Better Environment''. Flower Press 1993, {{ISBN|9780942256055}}

==Legacy==
''Wormania'' was featured on [[Red Letter Media]]'s ''Best of the Worst: Wheel of the Worst #14'', where the panel offered extensive commentary on the video, remarking on the production value, the music, and  Appelhof's positive attitude and happy demeanor, in addition to her clear passion for worms.<ref>{{Citation|last=RedLetterMedia|title=Best of the Worst: Wheel of the Worst #14|date=2017-04-11|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jtshsLOoMbM |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211215/jtshsLOoMbM |archive-date=2021-12-15 |url-status=live|accessdate=2018-05-02}}{{cbignore}}</ref>
